name: Endowment effect

evidence.basis: Kahneman, Knetsch & Thaler (1990) mug experiments; Thaler (1980) coined the term; integrative review Morewedge & Giblin (2015). Robust and widely replicated.
evidence.effect_size_note: WTA typically ~2x WTP for the same good; effect is real but its magnitude and interpretation are contested (procedure and market experience moderate it heavily)

evidence_terms: willingness to accept willingness to pay gap

pinned_evidence.title: Experimental Tests of the Endowment Effect and the Coase Theorem
The Willingness to Pay–Willingness to Accept Gap, the 'Endowment Effect'...
pinned_evidence.reason: dissent — Plott & Zeiler: procedures may explain the gap

mechanism_summary_for_context: Once something is 'mine', I value it more highly than I would to acquire it — parting with it is coded as a loss (endowment is upstream of LA-01). Ownership can be psychological, not just legal: having created, customized, or invested in something confers the effect. This is why trials, personalization, and 'your X' framing raise perceived value and resistance to giving up.

preconditions.reason: the effect requires a sense of ownership; it does not apply before the user has made, customized, or possessed something

applicability.culture_note: Ownership psychology is broadly cross-cultural, but what confers 'mine-ness' (effort, personalization, possession) and its strength varies; treat as an L3 surface parameter

implementations.generation_directive: Surface what the user has made as visibly theirs before any ask: 'Your gallery', 'Your workspace', concrete previews of their own outputs. Ownership must be established before LA-01 loss framing is applied (sequence EN-03 -> LA-01).

Have the user invest small effort early (customize, name, configure, pick preferences) so the product becomes 'theirs'. Investment creates ownership even without a purchase. Keep effort light and clearly rewarded — not a chore.
Frame the trial as already-owned access rather than a sample: the user possesses the full product, and the decision is whether to keep what is theirs. Pairs directly with LA-01-trial-ownership.

hard_rules.rule: Ownership language must reflect something the user actually created, customized, or possesses; do not fabricate 'your' where nothing was invested
Do not coerce meaningless effort solely to manufacture endowment; investment must carry genuine user value
If trial access is partial, do not imply full possession

constraints.boundary_test: Does the 'yours' reflect real ownership the user would recognize — or is it manufactured to create false attachment?

relations.note: Endowment creates the accumulated value that loss aversion then protects. Canonical sequence: EN-03 establishes ownership -> LA-01 frames its loss.
Identity/consistency overlaps: 'mine' shades into 'part of who I am'; distinct driver (ownership vs self-image)

Theoretically downstream of loss aversion; scored 2/3 on orthogonality — see dossier. Kept as a distinct L1 for its unique product implementations (creation, personalization) that LA-01 does not cover.

reference_examples.what: User-created designs shown as 'your designs'; the accumulated body of work makes leaving costly regardless of subscription logic
Personal playlists and libraries — user investment converts a commodity catalog into 'my music', raising switching resistance
Early goal-setting and personalization make the course 'mine' before any streak or paywall
